stem.en: The outer surface of a many-celled animal must protect the body from injury and germs. Which arrangement follows division of labour best?

text.en: A layer of similar cells on the surface that work together mainly to protect the body.
Outer cells that protect the body and also digest food, carry messages and make movement.

feedback.en: These cells switch between four jobs, so they cannot do any one job as well as a tissue that does only that job. This is the plan where every cell does everything.

text.en: A surface made of many different kinds of cells, each working on its own with no shared job.

feedback.en: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together. Cells of different kinds that each work alone do not form a tissue.

text.en: Any outer cells that happen to be there, since every cell of the body can protect it equally well.

feedback.en: In a body with tissues the cells are not all alike. Protection is the job of one tissue, not of every cell.

explanation.en: Division of labour means a group of similar cells does one main job for the body. A layer of similar cells that mainly protects the body is a tissue doing exactly that. Cells that switch between many jobs, or unlike cells each working alone, do not divide the work.

hints.en: Look for the choice where one group of similar cells has one main job.
